name: Device MAC address
plain: Blocked: apps see a fixed placeholder; Wi-Fi uses a randomized MAC per network.
meaning: A MAC is a permanent hardware ID. Android returns 02:00:00:00:00:00 since 6.0 and randomizes per network since 10; iOS 14 added Private Wi-Fi Address.

android.note: Returns 02:00:00:00:00:00 (API 23); null (API 30); per-network randomization default since Android 10

ios.note: Removed in iOS 7; Private Wi-Fi Address rotates per network (iOS 14)

limits.headline: Can't see your phone's real hardware address; apps get a fixed placeholder
limits.user_action: Nothing. Apps may try when they set up networking, but it fails
can: See a placeholder address (02:00:00:00:00:00) on older Android
See a different random address on each Wi-Fi network
Find nothing on Android 11 and newer
cannot: See the real MAC address on Android 6 and newer
Use the address to track you across networks (random address per network since Android 10 and iOS 14)
Get an address on iPhone; no public way exists since iOS 7
limits.differs: Android shows 02:00:00:00:00:00 and later nothing. iPhone has had no way since iOS 7.

story.what_it_is: Apps cannot read your phone's permanent hardware ID for Wi-Fi.

marketing.name: Private Wi-Fi Address
marketing.pitch: iPhone uses a different Wi-Fi address for each network so people cannot track it from place to place.

marketing.name: MAC randomization
marketing.pitch: Android uses a random MAC address for each Wi-Fi network by default to protect privacy.

story.for_you: You never see it. The phone simply uses a random Wi-Fi ID for each network, so shops and airports cannot follow you from place to place. You can turn this off for a network, but it is not needed.
story.for_makers: Makers used to read the hardware address as a perfect device ID, and ad firms used it to track phones. Now they must use other IDs that you can reset. Wi-Fi companies still try to use signal patterns.

use_cases.example: Marketers wanted to use a permanent hardware ID to match one phone across all apps.
Shopping malls used Wi-Fi hardware IDs to count visitors and see which shops they visited.
Analytics firms wanted a stable ID that survived a factory reset.
Network admins used MAC lists to allow only known phones, which now needs other checks.
Companies that locked Wi-Fi to MAC addresses must now use certificates or passwords.
Developers now use a resettable app ID or sign in instead.

story.android_note: Since Android 6 apps see a fixed placeholder, and Android 10 randomizes the real one for each network.
story.ios_note: iPhone shows a private address per network since iOS 14 and apps cannot read the hardware ID.
